program: Coordinated child-abuse response, trauma treatment, prevention and survivor support
priceScope: Conditional full annual-work health and signed household-resource reference; not calibrated portfolio expected value or marginal gift

what: Chicago Children’s Advocacy Center coordinates responses to child abuse across investigators, clinicians and family-support staff.
Its Family Hope Center offers trauma-focused therapies and caregiver support for children and families.
The organization also runs prevention and education work and has added services for adult survivors.
strengths: A named evidence-based therapy offers a plausible route from funded care to better child mental health.
Original returns permit a full recipient expense and donated-resource reconciliation.
Coordinated services and a central referral network can address practical barriers to care.
reservations: Reported child reach is not the number completing effective treatment or benefiting because of a gift.
The QALY conversion, program mix, local geography and funding elasticity remain judgments.
New program scope and unquantified other-portfolio net health could substantially change the result.

sections.what:
This report covers an ordinary unrestricted gift to the entire Chicago Children's Advocacy Center (EIN 36-4251865), not a restricted therapy purchase. The recipient coordinates abuse investigations, advocacy and family support, clinical care, trafficking responses, prevention and education. Family Hope Center uses several modalities, including TF-CBT, CFTSI, ARC and ITCT; it also supports caregivers and children with problematic sexual behavior. [Clinical services](https://www.chicagocac.org/what-we-do/family-hope-center/)

The portfolio has expanded since the financial reference year: Imagination Theater entered the education department in July 2025, and CAN Hope launched in November 2025 to coordinate adult survivor services. These activities belong in the ordinary-gift scope even though the quantitative channel below is child PTSD treatment. Retaining their costs while provisionally assigning their net health zero is an explicit incomplete-portfolio assumption, not evidence they have no value. [Program integration](https://www.chicagocac.org/imagination-theater-joins-chicagocac/) [CAN Hope](https://www.chicagocac.org/canhope/)

The edition counts health accruing to residents of the Chicago-Naperville-Elgin metropolitan area under OMB bulletin 23-01. Chicago location alone does not establish residence for every client or statewide training beneficiary.
sections.monitoring:
FY25's annual report lists 585 children and 154 caregivers receiving 7,035 therapy hours. These are reach and service measures; neither hours nor people establish distinct completed evidence-based courses, PTSD remission, or QALYs. The later return reports 7,034 hours, and also differs from the annual report on some investigative counts. The model uses the explicitly labeled annual-report child count, with a half-reach sensitivity, and does not combine the conflicting counts. [Annual report, p. 5](https://www.chicagocac.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/FY25-Annual-Report-Web-12.22.pdf) [FY25 return, Part III](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202631349349313328/IRS990)

The primary randomized trial compared TF-CBT with active child-centered therapy in 229 sexually abused children aged 8–14. Among complete posttreatment PTSD assessments, 19/89 TF-CBT children and 42/91 controls still met PTSD criteria: a 0.248055 difference in probability, calculated from counts. That is not a Chicago recipient estimate or a general-population prevention effect. [Cohen et al., 2004](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1201422/) The follow-up abstract describes persistent symptom differences at six and twelve months; it does not supply Chicago utility gains or demonstrate lifetime protection. [Deblinger et al., 2006](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17135993/)

Request linked, deidentified counts by residence, baseline diagnosis/severity, treatment modality, adequate dose, completion, wait time and repeated health outcomes; include non-completers and reasons for missing follow-up. Compare outcomes with realistic alternative services and track adverse events and repeat exposure. Privacy-preserving aggregate evidence is sufficient; identifiable abuse records are neither needed nor requested.
sections.qualitative:
A coordinated site can reduce navigation burden and link children to care after disclosure. The PATHH network maintains a central waitlist, considers slots at multiple providers, and supports families during the wait. This supports a credible access mechanism but also identifies alternative providers that remain in the no-gift counterfactual. A referral or an investigation is not automatically an averted abuse episode. [PATHH](https://www.chicagocac.org/education-outreach-prevention/community-partnerships/pathh-collaboration/)

Clinical evidence is stronger for one named treatment than for the effect of an unrestricted donation to the combined organization. We therefore separate trial-like eligibility, course completion, transfer to this setting, access to equivalent alternative treatment and funding additionality. All local proportions remain judgments. These parameters can be correlated; multiplying them does not produce a validated probability distribution.

Important unpriced pathways include caregiver mental health, family safety, medical linkage, investigation quality, prevention, trafficking response, adult survivor services and theater education. Benefits can overlap with the same child's therapy or with partner organizations. Possible burdens include distress from the process, disrupted families, ineffective referrals and displaced care; the report does not claim these harms occurred. Their net QALYs may have either sign, and the model explicitly tests negative as well as positive other-portfolio effects. Rights, safety and dignity also matter beyond QALYs.

An original four-site quasi-experimental CAC evaluation found more coordination and referrals, yet no observed difference in mental-health service receipt in the caregiver-interview subset. It also could not determine whether higher child-removal rates represented better protection or inappropriate decisions. This supports measuring follow-through and net safety outcomes instead of assigning QALYs to investigation volume. The older study did not evaluate ChicagoCAC or an incremental gift. [OJJDP original evaluation, pp. 5–8](https://www.ojp.gov/pdffiles1/ojjdp/218530.pdf)
sections.cost: Full FY25 recognized annual resources $11,750,254: PartIX $10,486,537 plus directevent $341,452 plus donatedservices $922,265. Unaudited annual-report $10,433,755 excludes net in-kind and is not substituted. Annual work removes the prior .5 marginal-gift financing factor; it does not prove next-gift expansion. Clinical health1.791803 and signed caregiver resources−.178236 combine to1.613567 equivalents, about$72.8M per better life versus original$131.2M. Original clinical effect/completion/utility assumptions remain conditional. 300 unique households, $20,000 baseline and $25 incremental annual burden are judgments, not observations; net assistance central0 is unquantified, not provenzero. Positive/adverse/unknown resource worlds retained. No speculative lifetime wages, retail therapy, duplicated stress welfare or success-discounted negative costs. Broader portfolio health and external economic incidence remain unknown. All15 original worlds are preserved as diagnostics.
sections.funding:
The FY23, FY24 and FY25 Form 990 Part IX totals are $8,897,281, $8,862,999 and $10,486,537 (three-year descriptive mean $9,415,605.67). They share the return-expense boundary, excluding donated services and fundraising event direct costs reported outside Part IX; this mean is not a future budget. [FY23 return](https://www.chicagocac.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/ChicagoCAC-FY2023-Form-990.pdf) [FY24 return](https://www.chicagocac.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/ChicagoCAC-FY2024-Form-990.pdf) [FY25 return](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202631349349313328/IRS990)

For the model, FY25 Part IX $10,486,537 plus direct event costs $341,452 plus recognized donated-service/facility expense $922,265 equals $11,750,254. Schedule D reports audited expenses $11,389,882, subtracts $922,265 and adds $18,920 of fundraising expense to reach the return total; the gross model then adds event costs separately. The $922,265 is not cash donated, and $98,765 depreciation remains in the accrual expense total. Neither this boundary nor its $10,827,989 version excluding donated services is a verified marginal cash price. Additional public investigator, hospital, partner and volunteer resources remain unvalued; the 25% add-on case is illustrative, not a resource valuation. [Return](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202631349349313328/IRS990) [Schedule D](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202631349349313328/IRS990ScheduleD)

The official annual-report presentation is unaudited and explicitly excludes the net effect of in-kind contributions/services. Its $10,433,755 expense and $8,989,770 ending net assets should not be substituted for the later return's $10,486,537 and $8,451,532. The tax net-asset rollforward reconciles using revenue less expense, unrealized loss and net donated-service/facility adjustment; the remaining source-specific revenue/expense adjustments and full audit notes need review. We inspected Schedule D's audit reconciliation, not the inaccessible audit PDF itself. [Annual report](https://www.chicagocac.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/FY25-Annual-Report-Web-12.22.pdf) [Return](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202631349349313328/IRS990)

Cook County approved up to $500,000 per year for 2024–26 with ChicagoCAC as fiscal agent for five advocacy centers; the whole amount cannot be credited as ChicagoCAC's own discretionary program funds. [County agreement](https://cook-county.legistar.com/LegislationDetail.aspx?GUID=AB57A607-9A39-4DA4-999B-63A0FE95A5A4&ID=6415142&Options=&Search=) Current job advertisements and a central waitlist show service demand/operations, but do not demonstrate an unfunded donor tranche. Obtain current accounts and restrictions, award renewals, reserve policy, capacity plans and a costed increment net of public replacement. The official donation route is verified; no gift was made. [Jobs](https://www.chicagocac.org/who-we-are/employment-opportunities/) [Donate](https://www.chicagocac.org/donate/) Current annual-work reference is separate from uncertain marginal gift capacity; historical donor-capacity assumptions are diagnostic only.

model.nativeOutcomes: Child/caregiver therapy reach, hours, course completion, PTSD symptoms/remission, safety, referral delay and recurrence; QALYs require unvalidated local mapping. Investigations, referrals and people trained are not automatically health outcomes.

inputs.name: C
inputs.unit: USD gross recognized annual recipient resources
inputs.rationale: Derived from FY25 Part IX 10,486,537 + Part VIII line 8b direct events 341,452 + Schedule D donated-services expense 922,265. Retains all programs, administration and fundraising, including accrual depreciation. Not a cash-flow or marginal-cost observation.

inputs.name: N
inputs.unit: reported child therapy recipients in FY25
inputs.rationale: Annual-report reach, not new enrollments, completions, TF-CBT-only patients or causal improvement. Deduplication across programs and fiscal years unresolved.

inputs.name: s
inputs.unit: eligible trial-like TF-CBT fraction of child reach
inputs.rationale: Assumes half the reported child recipients have comparable PTSD/trauma indications and receive TF-CBT rather than the recipient's several other modalities; recipient fraction unknown.

inputs.name: c
inputs.rationale: Chicago completion unknown. Trial 73% full twelve-session completion is only external context and does not establish this value.

inputs.name: e
inputs.unit: incremental posttreatment PTSD-free probability among complete assessments
inputs.rationale: Arithmetic contrast from 42/91 CCT versus 19/89 TF-CBT remaining PTSD cases; complete-assessment trial estimate, not Chicago intention-to-treat effect.

inputs.name: t
inputs.rationale: Halves external complete-assessment contrast for local fidelity, case mix and selection uncertainty. Separate from local completion, alternative-care availability and gift financing.

inputs.name: a
inputs.unit: fraction without equivalent timely TF-CBT elsewhere
inputs.rationale: Assumes other half receive equally effective timely treatment anyway. For credited half, CCT-like care is retained as comparator; no additional no-treatment gain added.

inputs.name: u
inputs.rationale: Central 0.1 is not a measured recipient utility. Australian 0.87 general-population/no-abuse comparator minus 0.61 PTSD equals 0.26; not an observed recovery gain. UK annual health-state QALYs 0.7725 minus 0.7386 equal 0.0339; the 0.032 stress test approximates rounded quarterly values (0.193 minus 0.185) times four. Neither context directly validates Chicago utility.

inputs.name: T
inputs.rationale: Finite two-year cap. Follow-up abstract supports symptom separation through twelve months, not this utility or year-two persistence.

inputs.name: p
inputs.unit: retained effect fraction per additional year
inputs.rationale: Half the first-year effect retained in year two; stops thereafter. Includes catch-up and recurrence in a simple stress-test assumption.

inputs.name: d
inputs.rationale: First posttreatment year undiscounted; subsequent year discounted 3%.

inputs.name: g
inputs.unit: Chicago MSA fraction of net modeled health
inputs.rationale: City-centered clinical services support high local attribution, but resident ZIP/county and theater outreach leakage are unverified. Applies to modeled health, not population share.

inputs.name: K
inputs.unit: USD net additional unrecognized partner resources
inputs.rationale: Conditional K=0; public investigators, hospital staff, volunteers and partner services outside recipient accounts may have material opportunity costs. Do not add recognized donations twice.

inputs.name: H
inputs.unit: signed other-portfolio all-population QALYs before donor response
inputs.rationale: Conditional H=0 does not mean no benefits: caregiver care, safety/investigation, prevention, trafficking, CAN Hope and theater may help or harm; overlap and displaced care must be netted. Signed +/- tests, not observations.

inputs.name: households
inputs.rationale: Conditional hypothesis documented in current uncertainty; no controlled local financial estimate or observed unique-household count. Gain and accessCost jointly net taxes, withdrawn benefits, childcare, commuting and lost work.

inputs.name: baseline
inputs.unit: USD net household resources per year
